sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### IceCube-261113A: no additional track-like neutrinos in either prompt search window

IceCube reported on **16 November 2026 at 15:43 UTC** a follow-up to the Gold-stream track candidate detected on **13 November at 16:48:28.482 UTC**. Excluding the alert event itself, the collaboration found **zero additional track-like events** inside the candidate's 90% localization in a **1,000-s window** (16:40:08.482–16:56:48.482 UTC) and in a separate **two-day window** (12 November 16:48:28.482 to 14 November 16:48:28.482 UTC). Both searches returned **p = 1.00**, consistent with no additional-event excess. [IceCube follow-up](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46307); [initial event report](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46275).

For an assumed \(E^{-2.5}\) point-source spectrum, IceCube quotes a sensitivity in \(E^2 dN/dE\) at 1 TeV of **3.4–3.5 GeV cm⁻²** across the 90% region for the 1,000-s search and **3.3–3.4 GeV cm⁻²** for the two-day search. For the stated declination and spectrum, 90% of detectable events would lie at approximately **10⁴–2 × 10⁶ GeV**. These are model-dependent sensitivities to an *additional* neutrino component. They neither retract the original Gold candidate nor establish or exclude an astrophysical source association.

#### GRB 261113A: independent prompt measurements and very early optical photometry

The burst occurred on **13 November at 14:31:02 UTC**. GECAM-A and GECAM-B follow-ups issued on **16 November** independently resolve the multi-pulsed prompt emission in approximately 70–6000 keV. GECAM-A reports **T90 = 8.2⁺¹·⁰₋₀·₈ s** and, over T0−2.7 to T0+6.9 s, a power-law index **−2.44⁺⁰·²²₋₀·²¹** with a 10–1000 keV fluence of **(2.85⁺⁰·⁵⁹₋₀·⁷⁴) × 10⁻⁵ erg cm⁻²**. GECAM-B reports **T90 = 7.4⁺⁰·⁶₋₀·⁴ s** and, over T0−1.7 to T0+6.5 s, index **−2.55⁺⁰·¹⁹₋₀·²⁰** with fluence **(1.07⁺⁰·³⁰₋₀·²⁰) × 10⁻⁵ erg cm⁻²**. [GECAM-A](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46302); [GECAM-B](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46301). The reported fluences are not identical measurements: the satellites used different time intervals and responses, so their numerical difference should not be read as physical variability.

MITSuME Akeno began three-colour imaging **1.58 min after trigger**. A 540-s stack centred at T0+400 s measured **Rc = 17.2 ± 0.2** and **Ic = 16.9 ± 0.2 AB**, with **g′ > 17.6 AB (5σ)**. This independently confirms the early optical afterglow at the previously reported position. [MITSuME](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46304). Glowbug on the International Space Station also detected multi-peaked emission from about T0−1 to T0+7 s, but its report is explicitly preliminary: the observation occurred during high radiation-belt background and the response lacks a detailed model of surrounding ISS passive material. [Glowbug](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46309). These additions strengthen the multi-instrument prompt and afterglow record; they do not change the secure **z = 3.580** redshift reported earlier.

#### GRB 261114A: a long burst at z = 3.716 with refined prompt energetics and a late optical limit

For the burst triggered by SVOM/ECLAIRs on **14 November at 09:33:13 UTC**, the refined ECLAIRs event data give an imaging-defined **T90 = 73.9⁺⁷·⁸₋₉·₃ s** in 4–120 keV. From T0−17.68 to T0+56.70 s, a power law with index **−1.58 ± 0.07** yields a 4–120 keV fluence of **(2.14 ± 0.20) × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²** and photon flux **(9.31 ± 0.43) × 10⁻¹ ph cm⁻² s⁻¹**; the reported uncertainties are 68% intervals. [SVOM/ECLAIRs](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46306).

Konus-Wind independently found a roughly **7σ** count-rate excess from T0+11.011 to T0+22.787 s. In 20 keV–10 MeV it reports fluence **1.64⁺⁰·⁶²₋₀·⁴⁴ × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²**, a 2.944-s peak energy flux of **1.61⁺⁰·⁷¹₋₀·⁵⁵ × 10⁻⁷ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹**, and photon index **−2.22⁺⁰·¹⁹₋₀·²⁴**. Assuming the measured **z = 3.716** and the stated Planck-like cosmology, the team estimates **Eiso = 4.70⁺¹·⁷⁹₋₁·²⁵ × 10⁵² erg** and **Liso = 2.18⁺⁰·⁹⁵₋₀·⁷⁵ × 10⁵² erg s⁻¹**; all are preliminary 68% results. [Konus-Wind](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46308).

VST/OmegaCAM observed the field on **16 November from 00:34:57 UTC**, about 39 h after trigger, and did not recover the afterglow in stacked images: **r > 24.1 AB at 39.43 h** and **g > 24.5 AB at 39.13 h** (3σ, 1-arcsec aperture; not corrected for Galactic extinction). At z = 3.716 the g band lies blueward of Lyα and adds little constraint; the r limit is consistent with extrapolating the earlier SVOM/VT decay, which predicts r ≈ 24.0. The non-detection therefore tracks ordinary fading rather than demonstrating an abrupt disappearance. [VST/OmegaCAM](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46310).

#### GRB 261115A: GECAM-B measures a short multi-pulsed prompt phase

GECAM-B independently triggered on the Fermi/GBM event on **15 November at 22:10:54 UTC**. Its approximately 70–6000 keV light curve gives **T90 = 4.0⁺³·⁵₋₀·⁵ s**. A power-law fit from T0−1.25 to T0+3.25 s has index **−2.23⁺⁰·¹⁷₋₀·¹⁵** and a 10–1000 keV fluence of **(6.8⁺¹·¹₋₀·⁸) × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²**. The on-ground localization is **RA 3.3°, Dec −26.3°**, with a **5.0° statistical uncertainty**. [GECAM-B](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46305).

This is a calibrated prompt-emission characterization, but the localization remains broad and the circular reports no afterglow, host or redshift. The measurement therefore confirms the gamma-ray event and its approximate duration; it does not by itself identify the source environment.
